sources: dossier=silent on Extra/ProducerMetadata specifically; design corpus=concept:n (inert bytes / inertness discipline) establishes the general no-payload-bytes rule the invariant is grounded in; doc=lineage-record.md Invariants line 26 stated 'All fields are scalars (no payload bytes)'; code=lib/runtime/lineage_writer.go LeafRunRecord.Extra and ClaimTerminalRecord.ProducerMetadata are declared map[string]any, currently unassigned by the writers (EmitLeafRunLineage/emitTerminalForensics); test=lineage_writer_test.go TestLeafRunRecord_TagDisciplineAndOrder / TestClaimTerminalRecord_TagDisciplineAndOrder pin Extra and ProducerMetadata as deliberate, ordered, tagged fields of the record shape (not stray/incomplete cruft), and the openlineage emitter reads ProducerMetadata through
note: The record type deliberately (per shape-pinning tests) carries open structured-metadata extension fields; the doc's blanket 'all fields are scalars' overclaims. Narrowed the invariant to the true load-bearing guarantee (hash not bytes, inertness discipline) while acknowledging the open extension fields, rather than asserting a closed-scalar shape the type does not have.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 18 mentions claim-terminal captures only version_id + sub-claim manifest, silent on cause-discriminator granularity; doc=lineage-record.md line 34 said the cause discriminator names three paths ('the error-policy give-up path, the sibling-cancel walker, or the parent-abandon recursive descent'); code=lib/runtime/terminal_decision_forensics.go emitTerminalForensics sets rec.Cause only for OutcomeAbandonSiblingCancel/OutcomeAbandonDescendantCancel; natural OutcomeAbandon leaves Cause empty and is discriminated via outcome='abandoned' instead; OutcomeAbandon itself is produced by multiple settled paths (auto_terminal.go, held_cascade_defer.go, runner_terminal_release.go, runner_acquire_postcommit.go, child_execution.go aggregateParentOutcome), not a single 'error-policy give-up path'; test=none contradict this
note: This is a stable, complete, non-self-declared-incomplete mechanism (unlike 442) — the two-value cause discriminator plus outcome-implied natural-abandon is the shipped design, not a gap. The doc's three-cause enumeration and the 'error-policy give-up path' label were simply inaccurate; corrected to describe the actual two-way force-cancelled discriminator with natural abandon carrying no separate cause value.

sources: dossier=silent (not a behavioral question); design corpus=the ok-planner self-containment rule requires concept bodies to be free of file/spec/path pointers, citing sibling artifacts only by slug; doc=lineage-record.md lines 30 and 34 both deferred 'concrete values and emit-site mappings live with the lineage spec'; code=the concrete values already exist as durable code identities (LineageOutcome* constants, TerminalOutcome, terminal-kind strings), so nothing is lost by dropping the pointer; test=n/a
